GUNPOWDER KINGDOM: DUNGEONS PLAYER FIELD MANUAL

The Kingdom discovered gunpowder centuries early. Its crypts, harbors and sky-forts now call for capable expeditions. This field guide brings the essentials into one place: how to build a reliable carry, improve your equipment, use abilities with purpose, and turn each dungeon run into progress.

FIELD GUIDE 01 / 09
Orders from the field

Start with a plan. Leave with progress.

Gunpowder Kingdom: Dungeons is a loot-driven dungeon crawler built around clearing waves, improving weapons and armor, learning how each weapon behaves, and pairing two equipped abilities to solve the room in front of you. A strong run is not only about damage. It is about control, timing, survival and using the right tool at the right moment.

THE EXPEDITION PRINCIPLE

Farm → Keep → Tune → Advance

Build one dependable setup before spreading resources across every interesting drop. Consistent clears create better opportunities to improve the gear that matters.

01Farm

Repeat content you can clear reliably and target the next useful upgrade.

02Keep

Compare complete rolls. Keep the pieces that improve your actual run.

03Tune

Invest Traits and tuning resources into equipment you expect to keep.

04Advance

Move into Trials and harder activities when your current clears are repeatable.

THE CAMPAIGN BRIEFING

Know what to work toward

Use this route as a practical order of operations. Each stage should make the next one easier, not just add another item to the inventory.

STAGE 01 EARLY GAME

Establish a dependable carry

Start by farming the Admiral dungeon and securing the Admiralty Brace. It is the early-to-mid progression anchor: a reliable ranged option that can carry dungeon clears while you build toward stronger Trials equipment.

STAGE 02 BUILD THE WEAPON

Learn the Brace's Chain Shot

Its 12-round magazine supports sustained pressure. Light the three strap lamps, then send the chained-ball shot through a packed lane to damage enemies along the path, wrap the farthest target and pull nearby enemies together.

STAGE 03 TRIALS

Move toward level 59–60 pistols

Once Trials are unlocked, farm for a high-level pistol that can become your main damage weapon. Judge the entire roll: level, damage, fire rate, magazine, reload, range, critical stats and Trait quality.

STAGE 04 ENDGAME

Specialize the rest of the arsenal

After the main pistol is dependable, build around jobs: grouping, room clear, control, sustain, defense and boss pressure. An Exotic is valuable when its perk solves a problem your main weapon does not.

THE FIRST OBJECTIVE

Make the Admiralty Brace your first priority.

Do not spend the early game chasing every weapon that drops. A reliable carry gives you the breathing room to learn encounters, clear rooms more consistently and collect better equipment without constantly rebuilding your setup.

The Brace is especially useful when you create a clean firing lane. Use your two abilities to control the room or open space, then commit to the Chain Shot when enemies are lined up. Reload during safe gaps instead of waiting until the room forces you to.

FIELD NOTE / 001CHAIN SHOT

Group first. Fire second.

  1. Light the lampsBuild the three-lamp condition before committing the special shot.
  2. Pick the laneLet enemies gather or line up so the projectile can affect more than one target.
  3. Send the chainUse the shot when its pull and path damage can improve the whole room.
  4. Reset safelyReload, reposition and recover during the gap before the next pressure spike.
FIELDCRAFT

Four habits that make runs cleaner

Build around repeatable decisions instead of reacting to every enemy one at a time.

01 / ROOM CONTROL

Shape the room before bursting

Grouping and control make damage more reliable. Pull enemies into a lane, delay a dangerous wave or hold a group in place before spending high-impact abilities. A burst skill is worth more when it connects with several targets.

02 / ABILITY DISCIPLINE

Equip two skills with different jobs

Use one ability to create an opening and the other to capitalize or protect the run. Avoid spending both at the same time unless the room or boss window justifies the full commitment. Keep a mobility or defensive option available when survival is uncertain.

03 / WEAPON UPTIME

Protect your firing time

Watch magazine size, reload time, range and how consistently you land hits. Reload during safe gaps, reposition before enemies close the distance, and avoid wasting a full damage window while changing targets or recovering.

04 / GEAR DECISIONS

Compare the complete roll

Do not keep a drop for one large number alone. Compare its full stat line, Traits, perk and role in your setup. A specialized weapon can be excellent for one job without replacing the reliable carry you use everywhere else.

EXPEDITION ACTIVITIES

Understand the purpose of each stop

The field manual is organized around the activities and equipment decisions that shape a complete progression route.

THE RULE OF THE KINGDOM

Consistency is a damage multiplier.

The best setup is the one that clears the room cleanly, survives the next wave and converts its weapon perks and two ability cooldowns into useful results. Build that foundation first. Optimize the details once the run is repeatable.

FIELD PROCEDURE

Run the Admiral farm cleanly

Keep the loop simple and repeatable. Every action should set up the next wave or protect your clear speed.

Repeatable dungeon loop
01 / OPEN

Start with a clean opener

Enter with your most consistent room-clear setup. Use an ability to soften or organize the wave, but keep the Brace ready for enemies that survive the opener.

02 / GROUP

Create a firing lane

Let enemies gather in a lane or choke before spending a pull, line attack or burst ability. Better grouping makes each damaging action do more work.

03 / FINISH

Remove the dangerous targets

Prioritize enemies that threaten the team or interrupt the room. Use Chain Shot when its path and grouping can affect several targets.

04 / RESET

Prepare the next clear

Reload, recover, sort the drops and keep upgrades that improve the next run. Avoid spending heavily on gear you expect to replace immediately.

KEEP

Build around useful upgrades

Keep rolls that improve your damage cycle, survivability or ability synergy. A weapon that makes your clears more consistent can be more valuable than a higher headline stat.

TEST

Compare before investing

Use Weapon Compare to inspect both weapons, then test them in the same type of room. Check reload downtime, target access and how reliably you can land the full rotation.

ADVANCE

Move on when clears are stable

Once your current farm is repeatable, push into the next activity and pursue a meaningful upgrade. Do not abandon a proven carry for an untested drop.

TACTICAL DOCTRINE / 01

The King's Execution

Boss window / burst
WEAPON FIT
Requiem as the tuned burst weapon; The King's Writ or Bellwether as a direct pressure alternative.
EQUIPPED ABILITY PAIR
ABILITY IAnchor of Night
ABILITY IIEclipse Domain
FIELD EXECUTION

Combat rotation

4 STEPS
  1. 01

    Build Requiem's five pipe charges on ordinary enemies before the priority phase.

  2. 02

    Anchor the group or target. The 4-second tether increases damage taken by 30%.

  3. 03

    Cast Eclipse Domain as the squad commits. Its 8-second field grants +25% squad damage and slows enemies in its 44-stud radius.

  4. 04

    Fire the charged Requiem fan into the window while both equipped abilities are active. Let the weapon carry the burst instead of waiting for a third skill.

FIELD NOTE

If the boss ignores Anchor or cannot stay inside Domain, save the pair for adds and use direct weapon damage during the exposed window.

FARM ROUTE / REPEATABLE CLEARS

The clean Admiral loop

01Enter with the carryUse the Admiralty Brace as the dependable damage source. Equip one movement or safety skill and one lane-clear skill.
02Shape the roomFight near a doorway or open lane. Let enemies path toward the squad before spending grouping or piercing abilities.
03Spend abilities togetherUse the first ability to gather, slow or expose the wave; use the second to capitalize. Avoid firing both into separate low-value packs.
04Reload during downtimeReload while rotating, collecting drops or moving between rooms. Start the next wave with a full magazine.

The fastest farm is the run you can repeat without wipes, long recovery pauses or wasted cooldowns.

CLEAR SPEED / ROOM CONTROL

Make every wave easier to hit

01Choose a firing laneKeep the team from spreading enemies across the entire room. Hold a doorway, corridor or open side where line attacks connect.
02Control before burstUse a pull, slow, suspend or shield to create a predictable window. Do not stack control before enemies are in range.
03Focus the threatRemove elites and dangerous ranged enemies before cleaning up harmless stragglers.
04Keep the rotation movingWhen a cooldown is unavailable, use weapon pressure and reposition instead of waiting for a perfect combo.

A grouped wave is worth more than a flashy ability cast that hits only one target.

BOSS PLAN / DAMAGE WINDOW

Prepare, mark, unload

01Prepare the weaponBuild charges or perk conditions on safe targets before the boss window whenever the weapon allows it.
02Set the teamReload, take a safe angle and make sure the squad can benefit from buffs or debuffs.
03Open the windowApply the target debuff or damage field first. Activate the second ability while the target is in range.
04Commit the burstFire the weapon's strongest sequence during the overlap. Save movement or defense if the boss is about to retaliate.

If the boss cannot be pulled or held, use control abilities on its adds and keep direct weapon damage for the boss.

SQUAD FORMATION / FOUR-PLAYER

Give every player a job

01 / AnchorHolds a safe front and protects reload windows.
02 / GathererGroups enemies and sets up line or area damage.
03 / DamageUses high output during control and buff windows.
04 / FlexBrings healing, movement or a second control tool.

Two abilities per player means each slot should cover a different job. Avoid a squad where everyone brings the same control skill.

Loadout Dossiers

Equip for the assignment

Loadouts & Squad Roles

Build around the job you need to solve. A clean squad has a front line, a grouping plan, damage during the opening and someone who keeps the team in the fight.

01 / Solo · fast farm

The roaming gunner

Early carry
WEAPONAdmiralty BraceChain Shot · dual pistols
ABILITY PAIRBlink + Crescent WaveMobility + lane damage

Purpose: keep moving through repeatable rooms while turning clustered waves into Chain Shot opportunities.

  1. Use Blink to cross hazards or leave a bad angle before the room closes around you.
  2. Let enemies form a lane, then send Crescent Wave through the group.
  3. Keep firing the Admiralty Brace until three strap lamps are lit; aim the charged Chain Shot through the densest line.
  4. Reload during the room transition or while moving to the next safe angle.

Best when you can control enemy approach lanes. Avoid spending the charged Chain Shot on a lone low-health target.

02 / Trials · pistol DPS

The executioner

Boss window
WEAPONLevel 59–60 pistolFive-Trait damage package
ABILITY PAIRAnchor of Night + Eclipse DomainTarget debuff + squad damage field

Purpose: convert a prepared weapon and loaded cooldowns into one deliberate priority-target window.

  1. Build the weapon's charge or proc condition on ordinary enemies before the priority phase.
  2. Make sure the pistol is loaded and the squad is in position.
  3. Anchor the target, then open Eclipse Domain as the group commits.
  4. Spend the strongest pistol damage while the target debuff and team damage field overlap.

Trait target: Focused Fire IV, Primed Powder IV, Expose IV, Empowered IV and Tactician IV. Crit is the alternative when charge generation can sustain the cycle.

03 / Solo · survival

The survivor

Safety first
WEAPONReliable ranged firearmConsistent safe-lane damage
ABILITY PAIRPhalanx Shield + SuspendFront block + hard control

Purpose: create enough breathing room to reload, recover and remove the most dangerous part of a wave.

  1. Face the main threat before raising Phalanx Shield so the incoming pressure meets the frontal block.
  2. Keep the squad behind the shield line while the weapon maintains safe pressure.
  3. Use Suspend on the pack or enemy that threatens to break the formation.
  4. Reload or recover during the control window, then re-establish the front.

Do not turn away from the wave while shielding. Save Suspend for the threat that would otherwise force the team out of position.

04 / Exotic · room clear

The gatherer

Pack compression
WEAPONGumball Launcher / Relic Engine / Apex Predator / RequiemArea payoff or charged burst
ABILITY PAIRSingularity + Tidal SurgePull + grouping

Purpose: make spread-out enemies behave like one target group so the weapon's full area pattern connects.

  1. Place Singularity where the largest part of the wave can be drawn into the same space.
  2. Use Tidal Surge to extend the pull and keep enemies close together.
  3. Fire the selected weapon into the centre of the compressed group.
  4. Let the damage land before using knockback or moving the pack out of the weapon's path.

The order matters: group first, fire second. Knockback too early can scatter enemies before the weapon's strongest hit connects.

Squad assignments

Front line / tank

Taunt Pulse • Phalanx Shield • Healing Rift / Night Swarm

Hold aggro, face threats into the shield arc and keep the fight in front of the squad. Place healing where teammates are actually fighting.

Group control

Singularity • Tidal Surge • Frost Wall / Anchor of Night

Collect enemies, hold them in position and call out when the group is ready for the damage window.

Main DPS

Level 59–60 pistol • Focused Fire IV / Primed Powder IV / Expose IV / Empowered IV / Tactician IV

Keep shots on the priority target, enter each phase loaded and spend the strongest damage during Eclipse Domain.

Burst / finisher

Requiem • Meteor Call • Thunderfall • Golden Volley • explosive Exotic

Save high-impact attacks for groups or boss windows; avoid spending every proc on low-health stragglers.

Support / sustain

Healing Rift • Siphon • Night Swarm • Phoenix Repeater • Sunblade

Place healing where allies can stay in the fight. Keep damage rolling while sustaining the team.

Three squad callouts: “Pack grouped.” “Anchor landed.” “Domain now.” These tell the party when the target is ready and when the strongest attacks should overlap.
Combat doctrine

Field Notes & Quick Reference

Small decisions that make the whole run cleaner: reload timing, perk triggers, ability spacing and target discipline.

Weapon discipline

Read the whole stat line

Displayed DPS: useful as a comparison point, but practical output depends on whether your shots connect and how often the weapon stops to reload.

Damage: per shot or projectile. For a multi-pellet weapon, the listed total assumes the projectiles connect.

Fire rate: affects how quickly the weapon can deliver its damage and how fast it builds hit-based effects.

Magazine / reload: determine how often damage pauses. Reload during safe gaps, not when the boss becomes vulnerable.

Range: an advantage only when you have a clean sightline and can hit consistently.

Critical chance / multiplier: evaluate together with the weapon's rhythm and the traits that support them.

Ability discipline

Make cooldowns matter

Group first: pulls and pins increase the value of lane attacks, explosions and weapon perks.

Control before reload: Suspend, Frost Wall and Phalanx Shield can create a safer reload window.

Stack the right effects: Anchor of Night's damage-taken increase and Eclipse Domain's squad damage bonus make a clear burst window.

Do not overlap blindly: stagger knockback effects until the rest of the area damage has landed.

Save a reset: Blink or a defensive ability can preserve a run when a room goes wrong.

Fast pick list

Choose by situation

NeedWeapon / ability picksWhy

Level 59–60 DPSPistol + five-Trait damage packageBuild a repeatable main weapon before specialist pieces.
Group enemiesSingularity, Tidal Surge, Anchor of Night, Admiralty BracePull, pin or drag targets into a tight formation.
Long straight laneCrescent Wave, Railstrike, Silver Vigil, MusketHigh value when enemies line up and the full path connects.

SustainHealing Rift, Siphon, Night Swarm, Phoenix Repeater, SunbladeRecover health while keeping the squad in the fight.
Defensive controlTaunt Pulse, Phalanx Shield, Suspend, Frost WallDraw attention, block the front, or delay the wave.
How should I compare two weapon drops?

Use the same activity, range and team conditions. Compare room clear time, boss time, reload downtime, missed shots, perk uptime and survival. Keep the weapon that improves the full run rather than the one with the best single tooltip number.

When should I replace the Admiralty Brace?

Replace it when a level-appropriate weapon with a stronger complete build clearly beats it in the same dungeon. Do not replace it just because a new weapon has an Exotic glow.

Should Tactician IV always be the final Trait?

It is the default steady choice. Crit can be stronger when the weapon and ability setup reliably generate enough charges to keep the rotation active. Test both setups in a full run.

What if the boss ignores pulls or control?

Do not force a control rotation onto an immune target. Save pulls, pins and slows for adds, then use direct damage, debuffs that still apply and squad buffs during the boss window.

How do I use kill-fed Exotic perks?

Build their counters on regular enemies, then spend the charged shot when a dense pack or priority target appears. Avoid using a charged trigger on the last weak enemy in a room if the next wave is about to arrive.

Endless expedition / Weekly gauntlet

The Tower

Eight dungeon worlds. One sealed room per floor. Every climb tests how well your squad can adapt as enemy pressure rises and the route keeps changing.

Squad recommended
The gauntlet

Every dungeon. One climb.

The Tower combines the game's dungeon environments into a continuous floor-by-floor gauntlet. Clear a room, claim the floor, and move straight into a tougher encounter. The deeper the climb, the more important clean roles, cooldown timing and reliable damage become.

8 dungeon pools5-floor mini-boss10-floor bossWeekly reset
THETOWER∞ASCEND / ENDURE / REPEAT
The rules of the climb

Know what each floor asks of you

  1. One sealed room per floorEach room is drawn from any of the eight dungeon environments. Expect the layout, enemy mix and pressure to change as you advance.
  2. Every 5 floors · mini-bossA mid-boss appears on each fifth floor. Keep cooldowns available as you approach the milestone.
  3. Every 10 floors · dungeon bossA full dungeon boss marks every tenth floor. Treat these as major checks on squad damage, control and sustain.
  4. The clock · 15:00 baseThe climb begins with 15 minutes on the clock. Each cleared floor adds another minute.
  5. Falling and recoveryA fallen player returns when the squad clears the floor. The climb ends if the entire squad falls before completing the room.
  6. Chests and item levelsA chest appears every 5 floors. Its loot climbs toward item level 60 by floor 30.
  7. CheckpointsA checkpoint is awarded every 10 floors. Checkpoints and the Tower board reset every Monday.
Climb doctrine

Build for a long run

01 · Dedicated damage

Keep one player on the strongest, most consistent weapon they can land under pressure. Do not sacrifice every safety tool for peak sheet DPS.

02 · Group control

Pulls, slows and pins become more valuable when enemy density rises. Group enemies before committing line attacks or area damage.

03 · Frontline / recovery

Use defensive tools to hold a safe lane, cover reloads and help the team recover after a dangerous room.

04 · Save milestone cooldowns

Do not spend both equipped abilities on the last weak enemy before a fifth- or tenth-floor milestone unless the room demands it.

UNDER CONSTRUCTIONStill building dedicated Tower strategies. More floor-by-floor builds and boss rotations will be added as the route is tested.
Best approach: climb with a coordinated squad. Give every player a clear job—damage, control, frontline or sustain—and call cooldowns before the mini-boss and boss floors.
